title: Appraisal Order Assignment, Holds and Due Date Movement
content:
**Appraisal Order — assignment, scheduling, holds and movement of the due date**

- The appraisal management company assigns an appraiser within the report type's assignment turn time in business days, and the inspection is scheduled within the report type's inspection scheduling period in business days after assignment.
- An order is put on hold only when the appraiser cannot get access to the property or a required charge is unpaid, and it is released when that is resolved.
- The due date moves only when the borrower or the borrower's agent delays access: it moves forward by the number of business days between the first offered inspection date and the inspection date the borrower accepted. Delays by the appraiser or the appraisal management company never move the due date.
- A report whose completed date is later than its due date is a late report; the number of calendar days between the due date and the completed date is the appraisal delay that other Larkspur policies rely on.

#### Due date movement — hypothetical cases

| Who delayed access | First offered inspection date | Inspection date accepted | Due date effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| The borrower's agent | A Tuesday | The following Monday (no federal holiday between) | Moves forward 4 business days (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Monday) |
| The appraiser | — | — | Does not move |
| The appraisal management company | — | — | Does not move |

*Late report, hypothetical:* a report due on the 10th of a month and completed on the 12th is a late report, with an appraisal delay of 2 calendar days; one completed on the 10th is not a late report.
